patch.objective: Using Cloud DNS and Cloud NAT

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Associate Cloud Engineer exam guide (PDF linked from the certification page): setting up a cloud solution environment (~20%), planning and implementing a cloud solution (~30%), ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution (~30%), configuring access and security (~20%)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. Four sections with the weights above match the course seed's units; subsections 3.3 'Managing networking resources' and 4.2 'Managing service accounts'; the guide names CMEK (3.2), Query Insights (3.4) and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (2.1, 3.1). The HTML page at cloud.google.com/certification/guides/cloud-engineer/ still shows an older five-section outline (Cloud Functions, Cloud Run for Anthos); the PDF is the current guide.

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud NAT: Troubleshoot configuration
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'If there aren't enough available NAT tuples, the dropped_sent_packets_count reason is OUT_OF_RESOURCES'; a five-tuple 'cannot be reused within the TCP TIME_WAIT timeout', so many connections to one destination exhaust tuples; fixes: 'adjust the minimum number of ports per VM', dynamic port allocation (doubles a VM's allocation when it is close to running out), 'Manually add more IP addresses'. The 'IP addresses and ports' page (read 2026-11-18): each NAT IP address offers '64,512 TCP source ports and 64,512 UDP source ports'; the default minimum is 64 ports per VM (static) or 32 (dynamic), and dynamic allocation scales each VM from a minimum toward a maximum. The gcloud flag names are authored renderings (the reference page did not load in full).
